I did implement this already. it tries the following files atm:
* (file specified in flag if it exists)
* roles/requirements.yml
* roles/requirements.yaml
* requirements.yml
* requirements.yaml

this can obviously be tweaked. I personally keep my requirements file as per the convention in the roles/ folder. But I like giving users the ability to have it suite their preferences.
As per the comments, I've removed the added cli arguments, and have it only run with `roles/requirements.yml/yaml`.

issue_context.title: Ansible Pull + Ansible Galaxy Integration
issue_context.body:
### Summary

Currently, it's difficult to use `ansible-pull` alongside `ansible-galaxy` roles, because there's no way (that I know of) to insert the galaxy install command from the requirements file between the git checkout and the ansible playbook run.

Currently, the only way to do this would be with some hacks such as providing `requirements.yml` out of band, running ansible-pull twice, or dropping ansible-pull altogether and running git, ansible-galaxy, then running the playbook directly (without pull)

I think this could be an excellent improvement over the current state of ansible pull, making it more useful for a broader selection of usecases. 

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

ansible-pull

### Additional Information

I researched online, and so far could find very limited uses of pull + galaxy roles.

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

I've created a PR with a suggestion for this. I ran into this the other day and it seemed simple enough.
I've added a argument to ansible pull (`-r`, `--role-file`) that is able to load a requirements file for ansible-galaxy.

Hi!

Thanks very much for your submission to Ansible.  It means a lot to us that you've taken time to contribute.

We discussed this issue again in backlog today, and unfortunately, we're not sure if we want this feature in the program, and I don't want this to seem confrontational.
Our reasons for this are:

   * Since you can run multiple playbooks with ansible-pull, the first playbook can set up any requirements. You can call `ansible-galaxy` from the setup playbook.

However, we're absolutely always up for discussion.
Because this project is very active, we're unlikely to see comments made on closed tickets and we lock them after some time.
If you or anyone else has any further questions, please let us know by using any of the communication methods listed in the page below:

   * https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/community/communication.html

In the future, sometimes starting a discussion on the development list prior to implementing a feature can make getting things included a little easier, but it's not always necessary.

Thank you once again for this and your interest in Ansible!
